correctness.rationale: For odd n the maximal sigma(n)/n is 624/315<2. For even n, positivity and the three-summand inequality reduce 4pq to 32 prime pairs, 2p^2q to 12 and 2pq^2 to 4, with explicit unconditional prime bounds. All omitted divisors are proper because sigma(n)<3n for the shapes. The standalone source independently computes full divisors, checks each surplus formula and all 165 unordered triples for each of 48 pairs; the exact output is 25 qualifying n and 32 witnesses, matching the published table. Finite enumeration is used solely after proof of global bounds.

value.rationale: The smallest nonsquarefree multiplicity layer with three distinct prime supports is a natural first classification target for the exact-three near-perfect problem. The complete 25-case classification with all 32 witnesses closes an infinite prime domain via sharp bounded inequalities, and captures multiple-witness phenomena emphasized in primary literature. It is more informative than recomputing isolated table entries and may guide higher-multiplicity classifications.
